factory1.name: Statewide fabric factory (jurisdiction-free layer acquisition + county atom writers)
factory1.purpose: Acquire jurisdiction-free layers (parcel geometry, boundaries, roads, flood, soils, topo, CAD rolls, owner, wells, rail, footprints, special districts) one source / one pass / blanket a state, and write them into the atoms store as county-scoped property atoms. Per-state cost is roughly constant regardless of county count. Produces the FABRIC the jurisdiction factory fills in.

reasoning: The upcoming map-backfill work — Q3 harvest take-list, Q4 address-to-parcel, Q5 CAMA structural data — is jurisdiction-FREE payload completeness over sources the factory already visits statewide. None of it needs a zoning district, a ratified setback table, an operator ratification gate, or a cert roster, which is the entire reason factory2 exists. Q3's Class A cluster (GEO_ID 158, BLOCK 151, MAP_ID 147, ABS_SUBDV_CD 143, TRACT_OR_LOT 142) is parcel identity and plat lineage read out of cad_property and txgio_parcel; Q5 is a routing-precedence change so bulk_primary:true actually routes to a CAMA export instead of silently falling back to StratMap; Q4 is a read-only normalization-and-index motion over txgio_parcel.situs_address (99.3% of 15,479,206 rows across 196 counties). All three are the same shape as the parcel-node sweep that just completed: enumerate counties from store truth, dry-run per county, verify counts, apply per county, checkpoint the manifest. The correct vehicle is the existing county writer family plus the frozen run_sweep.mjs driver with its county list and its CLI script name swapped — its input, not its code. Routing this through factory2's onboarding lane would import a ratification gate and a cert roster into work that has neither, and would be the rebuild trap in a new costume.

PROGRESS.JSON BOM TRAP — CURRENTLY CLEAN, RE-INTRODUCED BY ANY POWERSHELL WRITE. Verified this file byte-for-byte: head -c 8 gives 7b0a 2020 2273 7461 ('{\n  "sta'), no EF BB BF. But the recorded defect is real (_STATE.md line 15): a PowerShell write put a UTF-8 BOM on the progress file and broke JSON.parse. run_sweep.mjs loadProgress() calls JSON.parse(readFileSync(...,'utf8')) with NO BOM strip, so it will throw on a BOM'd file. If you hand-edit progress.json, write it from node (fs.writeFileSync) or strip ^\uFEFF on read. Never Set-Content it.

THE RESUME SKIP-SET HAS A KNOWN ONE-COUNTY-HOLE DEFECT. run_sweep.mjs computes 'already' as landed ∪ halted.countyFips. A county that HALTED but never LANDED is therefore silently skipped on resume — 48457 was exactly that (dry interrupted at the boundary) and would have left a one-county hole in a 254-county fabric that no count-based gate would catch, the same class as the Harris multi-shp truncation. The 2026-08-09 fix was procedural, not code: clear the halted object so the county re-enters the queue, back up progress first, record the clearance in haltCleared[]. THE CODE DEFECT IS STILL PRESENT. Any re-run must, before starting: assert every attempted county appears in landed, and clear halted after backing up progress.json.
